reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, wide-packet re-review batch 3, 2026-08-01

samples_reviewed.question_text: What number comes next when counting: 7, 8, 9, 10, ___?
What number comes next when counting: 5, 6, 7, 8, ___?
What number comes next when counting: 12, 13, 14, 15, ___?
What number comes next when counting: 6, 7, 8, 9, ___?
Arrange these numbers from largest to smallest: 20, 19, 22, 21
What number is marked on the number line?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Counting-on tasks like seed 42's '7, 8, 9, 10, ___?' answering 11 genuinely test sequential counting, but seed 50's ordering item asks students to 'Arrange these numbers from largest to smallest: 20, 19, 22, 21' while its recorded correct_answer is [19, 20, 21, 22], which is ascending, directly contradicting the question's own 'largest to smallest' instruction.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: 'Count up to 1000' is never approached: the highest number appearing anywhere across all 7 samples is 22 (seed 50), with no sample counting through the hundreds or approaching the stated 1000 ceiling.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The seed 50 mismatch between 'largest to smallest' phrasing and an ascending answer key of [19, 20, 21, 22] would directly confuse a Grade 2 student about which direction 'largest to smallest' means, on top of otherwise simple, well-pitched counting sentences.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Next-number sequencing (mcq/cloze at seeds 42-46), largest-to-smallest ordering (seed 50), and number-line reading (read_mcq at seed 55) together give three distinct task formats for the counting competency.

competency_alignment.rationale: All 7 samples do build the counting-sequence and number-order skill named by the competency, rather than drifting to an unrelated axis like arithmetic operations.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Every numeric value used across all 7 seeds (2-22) stays in the ones/low-twenties range; nothing in the sample set exercises counting into the hundreds or near the competency's explicit 1000 ceiling.
